{{See also|Lander-Green algorithm}}
{{No footnotes|date=November 2019}}
The '''Elston&ndash;Stewart algorithm''' is an algorithm for computing the [[likelihood]] of observed  data on a [[Pedigree chart|pedigree]] assuming a general model under which specific genetic segregation, linkage and association models can be tested.<ref>{{Citation |last=Elston |first=Robert C. |title=Elston–Stewart Algorithm |date=2005 |encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Biostatistics |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/0470011815.b2a05018 |access-date=2025-03-20 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Ltd |language=en |doi=10.1002/0470011815.b2a05018 |isbn=978-0-470-01181-2|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  It is due to [[Robert Elston]] and [[John Stewart (scientist)|John Stewart]].  It can handle relatively large pedigrees providing they are (almost) outbred.  When used for linkage analysis its computation time is exponential in the number of markers, in contrast to the [[Lander–Green algorithm|Lander-Green algorithm]], which has computational time exponential in the number of pedigree members.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Balding |first1=David J. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hFjNvMWBk14C&dq=about+the+elston-stewart+algorithm&pg=PA14 |title=Handbook of Statistical Genetics |last2=Bishop |first2=Martin |last3=Cannings |first3=Chris |date=2008-06-10 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-0-470-99762-8 |language=en}}</ref>
